q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most: 28 of 74 videos with a baseline (38%) were outperformers, versus 10 of 47 for mid-size channels (21%) and just 2 of 36 for large channels (6%).

Audience mood is mixed everywhere. Mid-size channels are happiest, with 43% positive and 31% negative comments (net +0.13, n=1,842 comments). Small channels are mildly positive at 40% positive and 34% negative (net +0.07, n=2,025). Large channels are basically neutral to slightly negative, at 38% positive and 38% negative (net −0.01, n=1,594).

So the small channels get the most breakouts with a lukewarm audience, while mid-size channels pair decent breakouts with the best sentiment.

Caveat: the large group has only 36 baseline videos and 2 outperformers, so its rate is shaky. These are associations in a comment sample, not causes.
sql: WITH v AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), vp AS (SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(outperformer) AS n_videos_with_baseline, SUM(outperformer) AS n_outperformers, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate FROM v GROUP BY size_group), cs AS (SELECT v.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_comments, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN v ON v.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.size_group) SELECT vp.size_group, vp.n_videos, vp.n_videos_with_baseline, vp.n_outperformers, vp.outperformer_rate, cs.n_product_comments, cs.pct_positive, cs.pct_negative, cs.net_sentiment FROM vp LEFT JOIN cs ON cs.size_group=vp.size_group ORDER BY vp.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a: First impressions is the only format with a meaningful sample (n=19) and it does fairly well: 37% outperformed their baseline, avg relative lift 2.46, and the most positive sentiment among larger groups (net +0.24). Full review and durability test both show a 100% outperformer rate, but each is n=1, so that's anecdotal. Explainer/tips (n=5) has a high avg lift of 9.98 but only 20% outperformers, suggesting one or two big hits are driving it. Comparison (n=6), upgrade advice (n=8), keynote recap (n=2), meme shorts (n=4) and other (n=2) had zero outperformers. Upgrade advice sentiment was positive (+0.25, n=8) despite lift under 1, while keynote recaps were notably negative (-0.55, n=2). Caveat: these are associations from small samples, not proof a format causes success.
sql: SELECT c.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(CASE WHEN p.outperformer IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(p.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(p.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, SUM(CASE WHEN v.n_product_side>=10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_sent_videos, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN v.n_product_side>=10 THEN v.pct_positive - v.pct_negative END),3) AS avg_net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN v_content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' GROUP BY c.format HAVING n_with_baseline>0 ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Why are some high-lift videos not ready to scale? Name two examples.
a:
Because their audiences are reacting negatively to the product, even though views are high. Both videos have net sentiment far below the typical +0.048 (across 152 videos).

Example 1: TechDroider's "iPhone FOLD Hands-On" (first impressions, macro tier) has lift 86.7 (8.2x relative). Among n=41 product comments, 12% are positive and 71% negative, for net -0.585. The top complaint theme is crease and screen quality.

Example 2: Time Travel Visuals' "iPhone Duo's Camera Disappears" (short, mid tier) has lift 496.7 (46.9x relative). Among n=50 product comments, 12% are positive and 68% negative, for net -0.56. The top negative theme is that Android phones did this first.

Caveat: n is modest for both (41 and 50), and the comments are a sample, so treat this as a signal, not proof.
sql: WITH pc AS (SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product, AVG(sentiment='positive') AS pos, AVG(sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments WHERE lang='en' AND trivial=0 AND target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY video_id), base AS (SELECT ct.video_id, ct.title, ct.format, cr.name AS creator, cr.tier, p.lift, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer, pc.n_product, pc.pos, pc.neg, pc.pos-pc.neg AS net FROM content ct JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=ct.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=ct.video_id JOIN pc ON pc.video_id=ct.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND pc.n_product>=10), typ AS (SELECT AVG(net) AS typical_net, COUNT(*) AS n_videos FROM base) SELECT b.creator, b.title, b.format, b.tier, ROUND(b.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(b.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, b.n_product, ROUND(b.pos,3) AS pct_pos, ROUND(b.neg,3) AS pct_neg, ROUND(b.net,3) AS net, ROUND(t.typical_net,3) AS typical_net, t.n_videos, (SELECT th.theme FROM comments c JOIN comment_themes th ON th.comment_id=c.comment_id WHERE c.video_id=b.video_id AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.sentiment='negative' AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY th.theme ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1) AS top_negative_theme FROM base b, typ t WHERE b.outperformer=1 AND b.net < t.typical_net-0.05 ORDER BY b.net ASC LIMIT 2

q: Inside the price discussion, which sub-topics are most negative and which are positive?
a:
Almost every price sub-topic skews negative; only one is clearly positive.

Most negative: regional price gap (n=142, net -0.845, 87% negative), overpriced for the tradeoffs (n=65, net -0.80, 86% negative), and cost jokes (n=61, net -0.754, 87% negative). Affordability barrier (n=81, net -0.654) and comparisons to Pro and iPad (n=33, net -0.576) are also strongly negative. The general bucket (n=190) sits at -0.547.

Milder or positive: storage, trade-in and financing is negative but softer (n=46, net -0.283). The Samsung Fold comparison is roughly split (n=78, net -0.064, 36% positive vs 42% negative). The only clearly positive sub-topic is "fair for foldables" (n=68, net +0.662, 72% positive).

Caveat: these are associations in a comment sample, not causes, and the smaller groups (n=33 to 68) are less stable.
sql: SELECT c.price_sub, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(c.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(c.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(c.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(c.sentiment='positive') - AVG(c.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id JOIN comment_themes t ON t.comment_id=c.comment_id AND t.theme='price_affordability' WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND c.price_sub IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.price_sub ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the iPhone Duo compare with the iPhone 18 Pro?
a:
The iPhone 18 Pro gets better sentiment than the Duo, though the gap comes from negatives, not positives. Net sentiment is +0.149 for the 18 Pro (n=2,673 comments across 92 videos) versus +0.064 for the Duo (n=5,461 across 167 videos).

Positive share is almost identical: 40.5% for the Duo and 40.3% for the 18 Pro. The difference is that the Duo draws more negative comments (34.1% vs 25.4%) and fewer neutral ones (25.4% vs 34.3%). Duo commenters are more polarized, while 18 Pro comments are more often neutral.

Both samples are fairly large, so the gap looks real. Still, these are YouTube comments on non-official videos, so they reflect who comments, not all buyers, and the numbers show association, not cause.
sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE c.topic IN ('duo','iphone_18_pro') AND c.format!='official' AND m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY c.topic LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about the Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
Praise centers on excitement and the fold experience; criticism centers on price. Hype and purchase excitement is the most positive theme (n=629, 90% positive, 1.6% negative), though it's about enthusiasm rather than a specific feature. Among product features, the fold animation and UI is the best liked (n=316, 71% positive, 20% negative). Android comparisons are also mostly favorable (n=1,170, 50% positive, 31% negative).

Price is the biggest complaint (n=764, 65% negative, 17% positive), followed by the idea that Android makers did it first (n=448, 63% negative). Apple brand and leadership comments lean negative too (n=363, 51% negative). Crease/screen quality, camera hardware and durability are mildly negative (n=349 to 431, about 36% to 41% negative).

Caveat: these are associations in a sample of 5,461 product-side comments, not proof of what drives opinions. A comment can also be counted under more than one theme.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.comment_id, c.sentiment FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor')), tot AS (SELECT count(*) AS total FROM base) SELECT t.theme, count(*) AS n, sum(b.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, sum(b.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg, round(1.0*sum(b.sentiment='positive')/count(*),3) AS pct_pos, round(1.0*sum(b.sentiment='negative')/count(*),3) AS pct_neg, round(1.0*(sum(b.sentiment='positive')-sum(b.sentiment='negative'))/count(*),3) AS net_sent, round(1.0*count(*)/(SELECT total FROM tot),3) AS share_of_product_side, (SELECT total FROM tot) AS total_product_side_n FROM base b JOIN comment_themes t ON t.comment_id=b.comment_id GROUP BY t.theme ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 40
